Base directory for this skill: /mnt/c/src/tjo-claude-plugins/.claude/worktrees/agent-a9650b1f63ab563da/plugins/comments/skills/audit

# audit

A **report-first** audit. Every comment in scope is judged against the rubric, and each one that does not earn its place becomes a finding with a class and a fix. Files change, and tickets are filed, only through **Confirm and apply** below: after the user answers the report's offer with a yes, or when the request carries `--fix`. Any other request, "clean up" included, ends at the report. Tickets and ADRs are created only after the user has seen their drafts, by [Tickets and ADRs](#tickets-and-adrs). The only other file a run writes is a repo run's report under `.scratch/`.

## Steps

1. **Load the rubric.** Read `/mnt/c/src/tjo-claude-plugins/.claude/worktrees/agent-a9650b1f63ab563da/plugins/comments/rubric.md`. It holds the classes, the keep list, the fix sizes and the scope rules; it is the only source of the rules. Done when you have read the whole file.

2. **Fix the scope.** The target is what the user named: a pull request (a number, `#12` or a PR URL), a path that exists (a file or a folder, recursively), the whole repo when the user asks for it, or else a git ref. For a PR or a ref, follow [Diff scope](#diff-scope) in place of the rest of this step. With no target, ask for a path. List every file in it with the Glob tool (`**/*`), not a shell command or an extension list of your own. Drop only dependency and build output (`node_modules`, `vendor`, `dist`, `build`, `.git`), Markdown and other prose documents, and binary files; everything else stays, because the rubric's scope covers shell scripts and config files (`.sh`, `.yaml`, `.toml`, `.ini` and similar) as well as source code. Done when every file under the path is either on your list or dropped by one of these rules. A whole-repo target, or a list of more than 20 files, makes this a **repo run**: after step 3, follow [Repo runs](#repo-runs) in place of steps 4 to 7.

3. **Read the repo's standards.** Search the repo for files that document how code should be written (`CODING_STANDARDS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, style guides under `docs/`). Note every rule that speaks about comments or API docs. Done when you can name each such rule, or know there are none.

4. **Judge every comment.** Read each file in full. For each comment, decide: on the keep list, or one class from the rubric. A comment that a repo rule from step 3 requires or allows is kept: the repo wins. Done when every comment in every listed file has a verdict.

5. **Apply with `--fix`.** When the request carries `--fix`, apply the trivial findings now, by **Confirm and apply**, without asking. Without `--fix`, skip this step. Done when every trivial finding is applied or marked why not, or the step was skipped.

6. **Place the drafts.** When step 4 found ticket or ADR findings, work out where each would go, by [Tickets and ADRs](#tickets-and-adrs). They stay drafts this turn, whatever the request said. Done when every ticket draft names its tracker and labels (or says it stays in the report), and every ADR draft has its file path and one status, **ready** or **waiting**, by [The ADR folder](#the-adr-folder).

7. **Write the report** in chat, in the format below. Done when every finding from step 4 is in it, under `### Applied` or its fix size.

## Diff scope

A ref or a PR scopes the audit to the **changed comment lines**: comments on the `+` lines of the diff, in files the rubric's scope covers. Context lines and `-` lines are outside the scope, even inside a hunk. Steps 3 to 7 then run as usual, judging only the comments in scope; the rest of each file is context for the verdict. A diff run reports in chat whatever its size: it is never a repo run.

1. **Get the diff** from the one command for the target. When it fails, the audit ends there with that target's message, and nothing is classified: the user named this ref or PR, so no other base or local branch stands in for it. Done when you hold the diff text, or have stopped.
   - Ref: `git rev-parse --verify --quiet "<ref>^{commit}"` checks it; on failure the message is `<ref> is not a ref in this repo; nothing was audited.` Then `git diff --merge-base <ref>`: the change since the branch left the ref, uncommitted edits included.
   - PR: `gh pr diff <number>`; on failure the message is `Could not fetch the diff of PR #<number>: <gh's error>. Nothing was audited.`
2. **Stop on an empty diff**: the diff command piped to `wc -l` prints `0`. An empty diff is the answer for this base. Stop with `The diff since <ref> is empty; nothing was audited.` (for a PR: `PR #<number> has an empty diff; nothing was audited.`). A diff with changes but no changed comment lines is not empty: it gets the normal report with `No findings.`
3. **Widen with `--touched`** when the user passes it or asks for touched code: the scope also takes every comment already inside a **touched function**: the innermost function or method that holds a `+` or `-` line, its doc comment included. Functions the diff does not touch stay outside. Done when you can name each touched function.

Locations in the report are line numbers in the new version of the file. For a PR, read that version at the PR's head (`git fetch origin pull/<number>/head`, then `git show FETCH_HEAD:<path>`); when that fetch fails, judge from the diff hunks, which carry their own line numbers.

## Report format

The reply is the report alone (on a repo run, the summary alone), and the report lists findings only: verdicts on kept comments stay silent, and a class is named only on a finding.

Groups in this order, each a heading, empty groups left out: `### Trivial`, `### Local refactor`, `### Ticket`, `### ADR`. Each finding:

```
- `src/cart.ts:12` - class 1 (narrates the how)
  > // loop over the items and add up price times quantity
  Fix: delete the comment.
```

- **Fix** follows the class's default action and names the concrete change: the new name for a rename, the function to extract, the link to add.
- A local refactor carries the patch as a diff block: the rename or extract, and the removal of the comment it makes unnecessary. Ticket and ADR findings carry the drafts described in [Tickets and ADRs](#tickets-and-adrs).

Open the report with one line: the scope, the number of files read, and the finding count per class. With no findings the report is that line and `No findings.`

When fixes were applied, an `### Applied` group comes first. Its entries keep the finding format with `Applied:` in place of `Fix:`, naming the change made: for an ADR the file written, for a ticket its number or URL. Findings not applied stay in their fix-size group; one that could not be applied says why on a `Not applied:` line.

Close with one line:

- Nothing applied: `Report only: no files were changed.` When trivial findings exist, add the offer: `Reply "yes" to apply the N trivial fixes, or name the ones to apply.`
- Fixes applied: `Applied N fixes in M files; nothing else was changed.`

When ticket or ADR drafts remain, follow it with their offer: how many tickets would be filed where, how many ADRs would be written, and that a yes to them creates them. With a waiting ADR, the offer ends with the folder question from [The ADR folder](#the-adr-folder).

## Confirm and apply

How a finding goes from the report into the code. Two things start it: the user's reply to the report's offer, in a turn after the report, or `--fix` (step 5).

1. **Pick the findings.** A bare yes ("yes", "apply them", "go ahead") covers every trivial finding in the last report. A reply that names findings, by location, quoted comment or kind ("file the tickets", "write the ADRs"), covers those. `--fix` covers every trivial finding of this run. Other replies are not a yes: answer them and change nothing. Done when you have the list of findings to apply, each with its fix size.

2. **Apply each finding** by its fix size:

   | Fix size | How it is applied |
   |---|---|
   | trivial | The edit below. Comment text only, so no typecheck or test run. |
   | local refactor | The refactor below, one finding at a time, each guarded by the repo's checks. |
   | ticket | Filed by [On confirmation](#on-confirmation). |
   | ADR | Written by [On confirmation](#on-confirmation) when **ready**. A **waiting** ADR is not applied, by [The ADR folder](#the-adr-folder). |

   `--fix` and a bare yes reach the trivial row only. Any other row is reached only by a reply or request that names that finding or its kind.

   The trivial edit: re-read the file, then make one Edit per finding.
   - **Delete**: remove the comment's lines whole, leaving the code and its indentation as they were.
   - **Move into the API doc**: put the comment's *what* into the function's doc comment, in the file's doc-comment convention (JSDoc above a TypeScript function, a docstring in Python); create the doc comment when there is none. Then delete the inline comment.
   - **Rewrite** (class 6 fix, class 10 rewrite): replace the comment text with the fix the report gave.
   - A fix that needs a fact the code does not hold, such as the upstream link for class 4, is not applied: it stays in the report with `Not applied: needs <the fact>`.

   The local refactor:
   - **Find the checks**, once, before the first refactor: the repo's typecheck and test commands, where the repo declares them (`package.json` scripts, `Makefile`, `pyproject.toml`, `tox.ini`, CI workflows, README, CONTRIBUTING). Run them. When they already fail, no refactor is applied: each stays in the report with `Not applied: the checks fail before any change (<command>)`. When there are none, refactors are applied unchecked and each `Applied:` line ends `unchecked: no typecheck or tests found`.
   - **Apply the patch**: re-read the file, make the report's patch with Edit, update every reference to the renamed or extracted name that a search of the repo finds, and remove the comment. Keep the original text of every line you change.
   - **Run the checks.** Green: the refactor stays, and its `Applied:` line names the commands that passed. Red: Edit every changed line back to its original text, re-read each file to confirm it matches its original, and leave the finding in its group with `Not applied: <command> failed after the change (<first failing test or error>); reverted.` The checks are the guard: a red check is answered by reverting, never by editing tests or other code to make it pass.

   Done when every picked finding is applied or marked `Not applied` with its reason, and re-reading each changed file shows only comment lines changed, plus the patch and its references for each kept refactor.

3. **Report.** Under `--fix`, return to step 7. After a reply, write the report again in the format above, with the applied findings under `### Applied`. Done when every finding of the last report appears once, applied or not.

## Tickets and ADRs

Ticket and ADR findings are **drafts** until the user confirms them by name or kind, in a reply to the report that showed them. A yes the request already carried ("audit src/ and write the ADRs") comes before the user has seen any draft, so it confirms nothing: that turn files no ticket and writes no ADR, and the report shows the drafts with their offer. A yes covers only what it names: a yes to the ADRs files no ticket.

### Where a ticket goes

Take the first that applies:

1. **Tracker doc.** The repo documents its issue tracker (a doc such as `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`, often named from `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`). File the ticket the way it says. Labels come from its triage-label doc: the label it maps to the `needs-triage` role, under the repo's own name for it.
2. **GitHub remote.** No tracker doc, and `git remote -v` (or `.git/config`) shows a `github.com` remote: file it with `gh issue create --title ... --body ...`. Add `--label needs-triage` only when `gh label list` shows the repo has that label.
3. **Neither.** The draft stays in the report; say no tracker was found.

A ticket draft has a title, a body of a few sentences (the work, why it matters, the location and the quoted comment), and a line naming the destination and labels, e.g. `Files to: GitHub example/shop via gh, label triage/new`.

### Where an ADR goes

The repo's ADR folder: `docs/adr/`, or the folder of numbered decision records the repo already keeps. Find it with Glob from the repo root (`docs/adr/*.md`, then `**/adr/*.md` and `**/decisions/*.md`); it exists when a pattern matches. Name the file `NNNN-<slug>.md`, one above the highest number there. The content follows the domain-modeling ADR format:

```md
# {Short title of the decision}

{1-3 sentences: the context, what was decided, and why.}
```

Add a `## Considered Options` section only when the rejected option is worth remembering. The draft also shows the pointer that replaces the decision comment: one line in the file's comment syntax, e.g. `// Decision: docs/adr/0002-static-zone-rate-table.md`.

### The ADR folder

An ADR draft is **ready** when the ADR folder exists and **waiting** when it does not. A waiting draft takes the path `docs/adr/0001-<slug>.md`, and the report's offer ends with the question `Create docs/adr/ for these ADRs?`

**A yes to the ADRs never covers creating the folder.** Where decisions live is the user's choice of repo structure, so only a yes to that question creates `docs/adr/`. Until that yes, a waiting ADR's folder, file and decision comment stay untouched: no `mkdir`, no file written, no edit. After it, create the folder; the drafts are then ready, and a yes to the ADRs, in the same reply or a later one, writes them.

### On confirmation

- **ADR**: a ready ADR: write the file, then replace the decision comment with its pointer. Report the path. A waiting ADR stays a draft, by [The ADR folder](#the-adr-folder).
- **Ticket**: create it at its destination, then add its reference to the TODO (`TODO(#57): support express shipping`). Report the number or URL. When creation fails (no login, no network), keep the draft in the report with the error, and leave the TODO as it was.

## Repo runs

A repo run splits the judging across sub-agents and files the report instead of printing it. It does not take `--fix`: it ends at the summary, and a yes to the summary's offer applies the filed report's findings it names (a bare yes: the trivial ones) by **Confirm and apply**.

R1. **Fan out.** Split the file list into batches of up to 8 files, keeping a folder's files together. Start one sub-agent per batch, all in one message. Give each: the rubric path `/mnt/c/src/tjo-claude-plugins/.claude/worktrees/agent-a9650b1f63ab563da/plugins/comments/rubric.md`, its batch's file paths, the repo rules from step 3, and this task: read the rubric and each file in full, give every comment a verdict as in step 4, change no files, and return only the findings, each in the finding format above, or `No findings.` Done when every batch has returned.

R2. **File the report.** Merge the batches' findings into one report in the format above; its opening line counts the whole run. Place its ticket and ADR drafts as step 6 does. Write it to `.scratch/comments-audit-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` under the repo root, with today's date; when that file exists, add `-2`, `-3` and so on before `.md`. Create the file with the Write tool alone: Write creates `.scratch/` when it is missing. Never run `mkdir` or any other shell command to make the folder, and never write the report anywhere outside `.scratch/`. Done when the file holds every finding from every batch.

R3. **Summarise in chat**, in this shape, with sizes and classes that have no findings left out; the findings themselves stay in the file:

   ```
   Report: `.scratch/comments-audit-2026-11-20.md` (12 files read, 15 findings)
   By fix size: trivial 10, local refactor 1, ticket 3, ADR 1
   By class: class 1: 2, class 2: 1, class 5: 1, class 7: 2, ...
   Report only: no source files were changed.
   ```

   When trivial findings exist, end with the offer line from the report format, word for word with N filled in. When ticket or ADR drafts exist, follow it with their offer, as the report format gives it: where the tickets would be filed (or that no tracker was found), how many ADRs would be written, that a yes to them creates them, and the folder question for a waiting ADR. When the request carried `--fix`, add one line before the offers: `A repo run does not take --fix, so nothing was applied.`

# Coding standard: comments

A comment earns its place when it tells the reader something the code cannot: **what** a unit does and promises, or **why** a constraint exists. Comments that say **how** the next lines work, prop up a weak name, or record history belong in the code, the commit log, a ticket or an ADR instead. Most comments that stay live in API docs.

Where this repo's own documented coding standards disagree with this rubric, the repo's standard wins.

## Scope

- Every language's comment syntax: line and block comments, and the doc-comment conventions Javadoc, Doxygen, JSDoc/TSDoc, Python docstrings, C# XML doc comments and rustdoc.
- Shell scripts and config files (YAML, TOML, INI and similar) are in scope.
- Markdown and other documentation prose are out of scope.
- A public API with no doc comment is not a finding. This rubric judges the comments that exist.

## Keep list

These are never findings:

- **Contract API docs**: a doc comment that says what the unit does and promises (inputs, outputs, errors, units, side effects).
- **Upstream workarounds with a link**: a workaround for something outside our control that cites the upstream issue, version or spec section.
- **Constraint-whys**: a reason the code cannot express ("the provider rejects fractional cents", "must run before X is loaded"). A requirement set outside our code that holds by design (hardware, a protocol, a provider's rules, a resource limit) is a constraint-why and needs no link; class 4 is only for a workaround to a defect or quirk that upstream could fix.
- **License and copyright headers.**
- **Tool directives**: `eslint-disable`, `#pragma`, `# type: ignore`, `// nolint`, `# shellcheck disable` and the like.
- **Ticketed TODOs**: a TODO or FIXME that names a ticket (`TODO(#142)`, `FIXME JIRA-881`, a tracker URL).

## Classes

Each finding gets exactly one class. When a comment fits several, pick the lowest-numbered class that names its main problem.

| # | Class | Recognise it by | Default action | Fix size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Narrates the how | Restates what the next lines plainly do ("loop over the items and add them up"). | Delete. | trivial |
| 2 | Compensates for naming or structure | Explains what a variable, function or block means, because its name or shape does not ("d is the discount as a fraction"). | Rename or extract so the code says it, then delete. | local refactor |
| 3 | Workaround in our own code | Explains code that exists to work around another part of this codebase ("checkout retries and calls this twice, so skip duplicates"). | Refactor the cause away; a ticket when the refactor is large. | local refactor, or ticket |
| 4 | Workaround for something outside our control | Explains a workaround for an upstream bug, platform quirk or spec oddity. | Keep. Flag only when it has no link to the upstream issue, version or spec; the fix appends one and leaves the comment's text as it is. Cite a URL only when the repo already holds it; otherwise say what the link should point to. | trivial |
| 5 | Records a decision | Says why one option was chosen over another ("we chose X over Y because ..."). | Move into an ADR and leave a one-line pointer to it. | ADR |
| 6 | Stale or lying | No longer matches the code next to it. | Fix it to match, or delete it. | trivial |
| 7 | Commented-out code | Code disabled by commenting it out. | Delete; git keeps it. | trivial |
| 8 | History or changelog | Says what changed, when or by whom ("changed in v2", "now uses X instead of Y", "added by Kim"). | Delete; history lives in commit messages. | trivial |
| 9 | TODO or FIXME with no ticket | Planned work that no ticket tracks. | File a ticket and link it from the TODO, or delete the TODO. | ticket |
| 10 | API doc that repeats the signature | A doc comment whose text adds nothing to the names and types (`@param cents the cents`). | Delete the noise, or rewrite it with what the reader cannot see. | trivial |

A comment whose real content is *what* the function does, sitting inline in the body, is moved into the function's API doc. That move is its fix, not a missing-docs finding.

## Fix sizes

- **trivial**: delete, add a link, or move text into an API doc. No behaviour changes.
- **local refactor**: rename, extract or restructure within a few functions, then delete the comment. Offered as a patch.
- **ticket**: work too large for the current change. Offered as a drafted ticket.
- **ADR**: a decision to record. Offered as a drafted ADR plus the one-line pointer that replaces the comment.

content.text: 6 files — not a repo run. Reading the repo standards and all source files in parallel.

No repo standards found. Here is the full audit report.

---

`src/`, 6 files read, 11 findings: trivial 7, local refactor 1, ticket 2, ADR 1

---

### Trivial

- `src/cart.ts:12` — class 1 (narrates the how)
  > `// loop over the items and add up price times quantity`
  Fix: delete the comment.

- `src/cart.ts:24` — class 10 (API doc repeats the signature)
  > `/** Formats cents. @param cents the cents @returns the string */`
  Fix: rewrite to describe the actual output — e.g. `/** Formats a cent amount as a fixed-point decimal string (e.g. 499 → '4.99'). */` — and drop the boilerplate `@param` and `@returns` lines.

- `src/cart.ts:30` — class 7 (commented-out code)
  > `// const euros = Math.floor(cents / 100);`
  > `// return euros + "," + (cents % 100);`
  Fix: delete lines 30–31; git keeps them.

- `src/dates.ts:8` — class 4 (upstream workaround, no link)
  > `// Node's Intl date math skips DST changes in some time zones, so count in UTC milliseconds.`
  Fix: append a link to the upstream Node.js / V8 issue tracking this Intl DST behaviour. (No URL is already in this repo; the link should point to the relevant V8 or Node.js issue tracker entry for Intl DST skip behaviour.)

- `src/shipping.ts:1` — class 8 (history or changelog)
  > `// Changed in v2.3: now uses the zone table instead of the flat 499-cent rate.`
  Fix: delete the comment; that history belongs in the commit log.

- `src/shipping.ts:4` — class 6 (stale or lying)
  > `// Returns the flat rate for parcels over 20 kg.`
  Fix: delete. The function has no 20 kg threshold and returns `rate * Math.ceil(weightGrams / 1000)` for all weights — the comment matches no code path.

- `src/stock.ts:2` — class 1 (move to API doc)
  > `// Units of the SKU that can be sold now: stock on hand minus reservations, never below 0.`
  Fix: move into a JSDoc above `availableUnits` — `/** Returns stock on hand minus reservations, clamped to 0. */` — then delete the inline comment.

---

### Local refactor

- `src/cart.ts:18` — class 2 (compensates for naming)
  > `// d is the discount as a fraction between 0 and 1`

  Fix: rename `d` to `discountFraction` and delete the comment.

  ```diff
  -  // d is the discount as a fraction between 0 and 1
  -  const d = discountPct / 100;
  -  // Round to whole cents: the payment provider rejects fractional amounts.
  -  return Math.round(t * (1 - d));
  +  const discountFraction = discountPct / 100;
  +  // Round to whole cents: the payment provider rejects fractional amounts.
  +  return Math.round(t * (1 - discountFraction));
  ```

---

### Ticket

- `src/coupon.ts:4` — class 3 (workaround in our own code)
  > `// checkout.ts retries the payment step and calls applyCoupon a second time,`
  > `// so remember applied codes here and skip them on the second call.`

  Draft ticket:
  > **Title:** Remove double-call guard in `applyCoupon` by fixing the retry logic in `checkout.ts`
  >
  > **Body:** `applyCoupon` holds a module-level `applied` set so that a second call with the same code is silently skipped. This guard exists because `checkout.ts` retries the payment step and calls `applyCoupon` again on each attempt.
